question: Should humanity beam powerful, deliberate messages at nearby stars, rather than only listen?
answer: Earth already leaks radio and radar into space, and anyone able to harm us could probably spot our oxygen-rich air anyway, so silence protects little. A deliberate, well-designed message is how contact could begin. If every species only listens, nobody ever hears anything.
move: Whichever side you took, the hinge is who has the right to decide for everyone.
ask: Which decision am I about to make that affects people who were never asked?
counterpoint: Our leaked signals are far fainter than a beam focused on one star, so transmitting does change what others can hear. Contact cannot be undone, and its risks are unknown. A handful of scientists should not decide for eight billion people, and meetings between unequal civilisations on Earth give good reason for caution.
reference: Haqq-Misra, Busch, Som & Baum, The benefits and harm of transmitting into space, Space Policy, 2013
